final_answer: BR could not answer this question from its own knowledge graph. BR holds a single ABIDE dataset node (ds:manual:abide, n=2226, CPAC/MRI, ASD vs control) whose only edges are generic metadata (consortium, modality=MRI, species=human, hosting repository, task labels) -- direct_publication_count=0 for that node, and neither the Di Martino et al. 2014 (doi:10.1038/mp.2013.78) nor the Abraham et al. 2017 (doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2016.10.045) paper exists as a node by DOI, title, or author search. Consequently BR has no representation of 'Analyst A', 'Analyst B', a leave-site-out CV diagnosis-classification result, a mean-FD motion-QC threshold, or any dependency edge between a QC choice and a downstream ML result for ABIDE. kg_verify_hypothesis on the QC->CV-result claim returned verdict='insufficient_evidence', confidence=0, with 0 supporting/conflicting/neutral evidence items. kg_multihop_qa over the ABIDE node (2 hops, 50 paths) surfaced only irrelevant metadata paths (e.g. ABIDE -> 'Down Syndrome' ontology tag, ABIDE -> hosting repository). BR therefore cannot say which of Analyst B's specific results (e.g., overall diagnosis accuracy, per-site accuracy, feature-importance maps) must be reassessed after Analyst A's QC revision, nor which actually changed after recomputation -- it has no record of this scenario, these analysts, or these specific published results at all.
